name: Devine Hall
use: Traditional residence hall in the Upper Quad (525 students across Hitchcock, Randall and Devine)
builtText: Dedicated October 22, 1966 as a women's residence
architect: Irving W. Hersey Associates (builder Davison Construction Company)

facts.text: Dedicated October 22, 1966 as a women's residence and named for Maurice F. Devine, trustee from 1949 for two decades, who helped draft the 1944 GI Bill.
Designed by Irving W. Hersey Associates, built by Davison Construction, designed from the start to be handicap-accessible, and linked to Randall and Hitchcock.
Home of 'the Niche', a large lounge with pool, ping-pong, kitchen and TV, and of the gender-inclusive Lavender community on the 4th floor; accessible showers and laundry. Address 11 Quad Way.
Part of the linked Upper Quad with Hitchcock, Randall and Devine (525 students in all), with an elevator, kitchen, laundry and indoor bike storage; no air conditioning is listed.

s19a.title: Ranking of UNH Dorms and Residence Halls

verdict: Five-storey 1966 brick block in the Upper Quad, accessible from the start but plain and without A/C.
notes: No licensed photo found. Reference photo 02 (UNH Housing) shows a five-storey flat-fronted red-brick block with white-framed windows and a small white classical door surround: plain and institutional. The builder is Davison Construction, not Blanchard Stebbins (that firm built Hitchcock and Randall).
judgeNotes: Reference photos show a flat institutional facade with a token classical door. Down from the old run on exterior (4) and condition (4, no renovation or A/C).
